fit_reason: Owns 30,000 miles of natural gas pipelines (including Transco), 29 processing plants and gathering systems in Marcellus, Haynesville and other basins. Gas processing, gathering and transmission is where the gas shortage sits, and it is among the largest US gas pipeline operators.

Geothermal and recovered-energy power producer that also manufactures geothermal plant equipment and energy storage. Advanced geothermal is the most promising non-gas near-term power source (runs constantly, zero emissions), and geothermal is central to the business; one of the few established pure plays.

Operates about 83,000 miles of pipelines, including the largest US natural gas transmission network, with gathering, processing, storage and LNG facilities. Moving gas is central to the business and it is a leading US gas infrastructure operator.

Builds and rents natural gas compression and modular gas processing equipment and supplies electric power generation equipment for gas-fired power. Hits both gas gathering/processing capacity and on-site power; compression and processing are central to the business.
Makes solid-oxide fuel cell servers that turn natural gas into electricity on site, sold for data centers among other uses. Direct on-site, no-grid-wait power from gas, and central to the business.

Makes gas and steam turbines, nuclear and hydro equipment, grid infrastructure and storage systems. A leading supplier of the generation equipment for new gas-fired power, with power and grid equipment central to the business.

Provides on-site power generation and oilfield infrastructure, shifting toward natural-gas-fired generation fleets for large power users. On-site gas power to skip the grid wait is central to its growth.

Natural gas gathering and processing, NGL fractionation and gas pipelines (17,500 miles of gathering lines). Gas and NGL processing infrastructure is the core business and it is a top-tier midstream operator.
Large Permian-focused gas gatherer and processor with 28,400 miles of pipeline and 42 processing plants, plus NGL logistics. The gathering and processing bottleneck is its core business.
Largest US natural gas producer, with about 1.7 million acres in the Marcellus. Pure-play gas supply, with the most direct volume exposure to gas power demand growth.
Large US gas producer (Marcellus and Haynesville) formerly Chesapeake. Gas is essentially the whole business, with a major position in the Haynesville near LNG and power demand.
Appalachian gas and NGL producer with its own gathering lines and compressor stations. Core business is gas supply, with 17.7 Tcfe of reserves.
Appalachian gas and NGL producer selling to utilities, power and industrial customers. Gas is the core of the business and it has a large Marcellus acreage position.
Appalachian gas producer that also owns about 2,600 miles of gathering pipelines and processing facilities. Gas production plus midstream integration, central to the business.
Pure-play Haynesville and Bossier gas producer. Gas supply near Gulf Coast LNG and power demand is the entire business.

Interstate and intrastate gas pipelines, storage, gathering, compression and treatment in Appalachia and the Midwest, serving gas-fired power generators among others. Pipeline and gathering capacity is the core business.

One of the largest US midstream companies, with gas processing, NGL pipelines and fractionation, and natural gas pipelines and storage. Gas and NGL infrastructure is central, though crude and petrochemicals are meaningful too.
Owns and operates the Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi LNG terminals and connecting pipelines. LNG export is the whole business and it is the largest US LNG exporter, adding demand for US gas.
Owns the Sabine Pass LNG liquefaction and export complex and a 94-mile pipeline. LNG export is the whole business and the volume driver for US gas demand.
Builds and operates large LNG production facilities on the US Gulf Coast (Calcasieu, Plaquemines, CP2). LNG is the whole business, adding to gas demand growth.
Operates a 93,300 km natural gas pipeline network, 535 Bcf of storage and about 4,300 MW of gas and nuclear generation. Gas transmission is the core business, with a power segment on top.

North American pipeline giant with gas transmission, gathering and processing, gas utility and renewable power including geothermal. Gas infrastructure is a large part of the business alongside crude pipelines.
Gathers, processes and fractionates natural gas and NGLs across major basins, plus crude and refined product logistics. Gas processing is one of two core segments.
Gathers, compresses, treats and processes natural gas and NGLs in Texas, New Mexico, the Rockies and Pennsylvania. Gas gathering and processing is the entire business.
Gathers and processes natural gas in the Bakken, including the Tioga gas plant and fractionation. Gas gathering and processing is central to the business, though the customer base is concentrated.
Midstream operator in the Delaware Basin gathering, compressing and processing natural gas. Permian gas takeaway and processing is the entire business.
Antero Midstream gathers and compresses natural gas in the Appalachian Basin, tied largely to one producer. Gas gathering and compression is the core business.
Contract natural gas compression operator in the US. Compression is needed to gather and move gas, and it is the entire business.
Owns and operates a fleet of natural gas compression equipment under contract. Compression capacity is a bottleneck for moving gas and is the entire business.

Large independent power producer (about 38,700 MW across gas, nuclear, coal, solar and storage) plus retail electricity. A leading generator positioned for data center demand, with generation central to the business.

Largest US nuclear fleet operator (32,400 MW including nuclear, gas, wind, solar and hydro). Reliable carbon-free generation is the core business and it is a leading player in nuclear power for data centers.
Independent power producer with about 18,000 MW of gas, coal, nuclear and solar generation plus retail electricity and on-site solutions. Generation is central to the business.
Independent power producer with about 10.7 GW of nuclear, gas and other generation, developing battery storage. Generation is the whole business and it is exposed to data center power demand.
Gas turbines, generators, HVDC and grid equipment, and wind turbines. Gas turbines for new power plants and grid equipment are central to the business.
Developer of small modular reactor technology (VOYGR, 77 MW modules). Nuclear is the whole business, though it is pre-revenue-scale and a longer-dated source of power.

Makes reciprocating engines, generator sets, gas turbines and gas compressors alongside heavy equipment. Gensets and gas turbines supply on-site power and are a growing part of the business, but construction and mining are larger.

Largest US utility by market value, with about 28,500 MW of generation, a large renewable and storage development arm, and a Florida regulated utility. Generating and delivering electricity is the whole business.

Regulated electric and gas utility serving about 8.7 million customers, with gas pipelines, nuclear, solar and storage generation. Delivering and generating power is the core business in a fast-growing data center region.
Regulated electric utility with about 50,000 MW of capacity and gas distribution, serving the Carolinas, Florida and the Midwest. Generating and delivering power is the core business.
Global power generator (about 31,000 MW) across gas, coal, hydro, wind, solar and storage, plus utilities. Generation and storage are the core business, with an energy storage partnership in Fluence.
Natural gas and NGL producer with midstream gathering and processing. Gas is the whole business, though smaller than the major gas producers.
Natural gas-weighted independent producer on the Louisiana Gulf Coast and Appalachia. Gas production is the core business.
Owns and operates a large base of mature Appalachian gas wells and gathering infrastructure. Gas production is the core business, but it is a low-growth acquirer of declining wells.
Integrated gas company with Appalachian gas production, interstate pipeline and storage, gathering and a gas utility. Gas is the entire business across several parts of the chain.
Generator with hydro, wind, solar and gas plants in Canada, the US and Australia, plus gas pipelines. Power generation is the whole business and it supplies data center power in Alberta.

Largest US specialty contractor for transmission, substations and power plants, plus pipelines, renewable and storage construction. Building the power and gas delivery infrastructure is the core business.
Major uranium miner and nuclear fuel services provider. Nuclear fuel is the entire business and the key listed uranium supplier, though nuclear power for data centers is a longer-dated source.
Makes thin-film solar modules for utility-scale projects. Solar generation hardware is the entire business, though solar needs land, transmission and storage at scale.
Provides grid-scale energy storage systems and software for utilities and renewable developers. Storage is the entire business and demand follows grid and solar buildout.
Energy generation and storage segment sells Megapack and solar systems to utilities and others. Storage is a meaningful but secondary part of a business dominated by vehicles.
Contracted renewable and gas generation owner with about 5,000 MW of wind and solar and about 2,500 MW of gas. Power generation is the entire business.

Makes naval reactors, nuclear fuel and commercial nuclear components such as steam generators, and is working on advanced reactor technology. Nuclear components are central to the business, though the Navy is the largest customer.
Makes diesel and natural gas engines plus standby and prime power generators. Power generation systems are a meaningful segment, but trucks and engines are larger.
Makes standby and industrial generators up to 3,250 kW for data centers and others, plus energy storage. On-site backup power is central, though residential demand is the largest piece.

Makes natural gas and other fuel engines and custom power generation systems used for standby, prime power and microgrids. Gas gensets are a meaningful part of the mix alongside industrial and on-road engines.

Engineering and construction firm that builds gas-fired and renewable power plants (about 15 GW of projects). Power plant construction is its largest segment and benefits from new gas generation demand.
Owns hydro, wind, solar and storage generation across North America, Colombia and Brazil. Renewable power generation is the whole business.
Canadian pipeline and facilities operator with NGL fractionation, gas processing and transmission pipelines. Gas liquids infrastructure is a large part of the business alongside oil pipelines.
Argentine gas transporter with a 5,769-mile pipeline network, NGL production and compression. Gas transport and processing is the core business, but it is concentrated in Argentina.

fit_reason: Large US shale producer of crude, NGLs and gas with gathering and processing. Gas is a meaningful but secondary part of an oil-weighted portfolio.
Global producer of crude, gas, LNG and NGLs with several LNG projects. Gas and LNG are a meaningful part of an oil-weighted business.
US shale producer of oil, gas and NGLs. Gas is a meaningful but secondary part of an oil-weighted business.
Delaware Basin and Haynesville producer with a midstream segment for gas processing and gathering. Gas processing is a meaningful but secondary part of an oil-weighted business.
Oil and gas producer with a midstream segment that gathers, processes and transports gas and NGLs. Midstream is a meaningful but secondary part of the business.
Hydraulic fracturing provider that has been building a power generation business for on-site power. Power is a growing but minority part of a frac-dominated business, per what I know of the company.
Australian producer and marketer of LNG, pipeline gas and crude. LNG and gas are a large share of the business.
Integrated major with LNG liquefaction and gas production. Gas and LNG are a meaningful part of a mostly oil business.
Integrated major and one of the largest LNG players, with power trading and solar. LNG is a meaningful part of a diversified business.
Integrated major with a large LNG chain, power generation, solar and storage. Gas and power are a meaningful part of a diversified business.
Norwegian integrated company supplying gas to Europe, with midstream and renewables. Gas is a meaningful part of an oil-weighted business.
Italian integrated company with a global gas and LNG portfolio and a retail power and renewables segment. Gas and power are a meaningful part of the business.
Oilfield services plus industrial energy technology for LNG, pipelines, gas storage and distributed power equipment. Gas equipment is a meaningful part of a mostly oilfield business.
Crude oil pipelines plus a gas processing and NGL fractionation segment. NGL infrastructure is a meaningful but secondary part of the business.

Oil and gas producer that manages gathering, processing and transmission infrastructure in West Texas and owns interests in Permian takeaway pipelines. Gas infrastructure is a meaningful part of an oil-weighted business.
Provides floating LNG regasification, terminals and gas supply for power generation projects. LNG import infrastructure is the core business, though it is focused on importing markets.
Provides floating LNG liquefaction and regasification vessels and LNG carriers. Marine LNG infrastructure is the core business.
Operates 13 LNG carriers. LNG shipping is the entire business but only moves gas rather than producing or processing it.

Diversified infrastructure with 61,000 km of power lines, 15,000 km of gas pipelines, gas gathering and processing, and data centers. Gas and power delivery are a large part of a diversified portfolio.

Regulated utility in the Gulf South with about 26,000 MW of generation (6,000 MW nuclear) serving 3 million customers. Generating and delivering electricity is the core business, in a region with large data center buildout.
Regulated electric and gas utility in Virginia and the Carolinas, which includes the largest data center market. Generating and delivering power is the core business.
Large regulated electric utility with generation, a large transmission network and wholesale supply. Generating and delivering power is the core business.
Regulated electric and gas utility serving about 3.7 million electric customers across eight states. Generating and delivering power is the core business.
Utility holding company focused on electric and gas transmission and distribution, with generation exposure. Delivering power is the core business.
Northeast utility with large electric transmission and distribution plus gas distribution and solar. Delivering power is the core business.
Michigan electric utility (2.3 million customers) with gas utility and pipelines. Generating and delivering power is the core business.
Wisconsin and Illinois electric and gas utility with electric transmission and renewable generation. Delivering power is the core business.
Supplies enriched uranium fuel (SWU) to nuclear utilities and develops US centrifuge enrichment. Nuclear fuel is the entire business, though it is a longer-dated power source.
US uranium miner developing in-situ recovery projects. Uranium supply is the entire business, though it is pre-scale and a longer-dated power source.
Largest battery maker, supplying cells and containerized storage systems for EVs and grid storage. Energy storage is a growing but secondary part of an EV-weighted business.
Makes industrial batteries and UPS and energy systems for telecom, data centers and large-scale storage. Stored energy is the whole business, though it skews to industrial applications.
Missouri and Illinois utility with coal, nuclear and gas generation, electric transmission and gas distribution. Generating and delivering power is the core business.
Michigan electric and gas utility with an independent power segment, battery facilities and transmission. Generating and delivering power is the core business.
Houston-area electric transmission and distribution plus gas utilities. Delivering power is the core business, in the fast-growing Texas market.
Regulated electric, gas and steam utility serving New York City. Delivering power is the core business, but it is a slow-growth territory.
Regulated electric distribution and transmission utility with about 24,000 circuit miles of transmission. Delivering power is the core business.
Kansas and Missouri integrated electric utility with about 10,100 circuit miles of transmission. Generating and delivering power is the core business.
New England electric transmission and distribution and gas utility. Delivering power is the core business.
Iowa and Wisconsin electric and gas utility. Generating and delivering power is the core business.
California electric utility serving about 15 million people. Delivering power is the core business, though wildfire liability weighs on it.
California electric and gas utility. Delivering power is the core business, though wildfire liability weighs on it.
